plain_english_revision: This amendment establishes a regulatory framework that exempts specific food vendors from standard Mobile County Health Department rules during regional celebrations, traditions, or cultural events. It defines 'intermittent' establishments as those not operating in their regular line of business for more than three consecutive days per week and requires them to submit an online application at no charge five business days prior to the event. The amendment explicitly excludes low-acid home-canned foods from these exemptions but allows churches conducting fundraiser sales on-site and bars boiling crawfish outside as exempt entities, provided they meet specific health requirements like having food handlers cards and waste containment plans.
candidate_position_supported: The amendment advances a policy of expanding regulatory exemptions for non-commercial or culturally significant food vendors during special events while maintaining baseline safety standards through application processes, site-specific restrictions (e.g., no home-canned goods), and limits on the number of annual exemptions per location.
evidence_quotes: An intermittent food service establishment shall complete an online application... for an exemption of food service at a temporary exempt event.

Other than as provided for in this section, the Mobile County Health Department shall not regulate an intermittent food service establishment that prepares food in association with a regional celebration, tradition, or cultural event

Notwithstanding Section 2, a church that is tax exempt and that conducts intermittent food sales for fund raisers... shall be exempt from the regulatory requirements of the Mobile County Health Department
